problems.name: Composites Among $[\xi 7^n]$ and Right-Truncatable Primes in Base 7
problems.statement: For every real $\xi>0$ the sequence of integer parts $[\xi 7^{n}]$, $n=0,1,2,\dots$, contains infinitely many composite numbers. Second, there is no infinite right truncatable prime in base 7.
problems.posedBy: Forman and Shapiro (1967), Dubickas and Novikas (2005)
problems.aiRole: The source reports an AI-produced computational route, certificate, Lean formalization, and draft under human direction.
problems.verificationNote: VibeMathed reports a source audit with a documented native_decide boundary; VibeMath did not compile or independently audit it.

links.label: Lean development, data and generating programs

problems.name: Erdős's Planar Unit Distance Conjecture
problems.statement: Erdős conjectured an $n^{1+o(1)}$ upper bound on the number of unit-distance pairs among $n$ points in the plane. A construction with more than $n^{1.014}$ pairs disproves that conjectured asymptotic upper bound; the exact extremal unit-distance problem remains open.
problems.resultNote: The asymptotic conjecture was disproved; this does not determine the exact unit-distance extremal function.
problems.model: OpenAI frontier model (specific version not disclosed)
problems.aiRole: Model-assisted construction of a point configuration reported to have more than $n^{1.014}$ unit-distance pairs.
problems.verificationNote: VibeMathed reports human expert verification and an arXiv write-up; VibeMath preserves that label as a source assertion.
problems.sourceName: Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture

problems.name: The Quartic Hessian Conjecture in Dimension Four
problems.statement: The Hessian conjecture is open exactly in dimension four. The source reports a proof for every quartic polynomial in dimension four, a proper slice of the full open problem.
problems.posedBy: The Hessian conjecture (de Bondt, van den Essen line)
problems.model: GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude Fable 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro
problems.aiRole: The source credits AI systems with exploring candidate arguments, adversarial review, algebraic checking, and editorial assistance.
problems.verificationNote: VibeMathed reports a days-old sole-author preprint and no independent review.
problems.sourceName: The Quartic Hessian Conjecture in Dimension Four

problems.name: Erdős Problem #267
problems.statement: If $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ with $n_{k+1}/n_k\ge c>1$, must $\sum_k 1/F_{n_k}$ be irrational? The proposed proof closes the range $1<c<2$ left open by earlier criteria.
problems.aiRole: Produced by the GPT-5.6 starships pipeline with Claude Fable 5 as reviewer, according to the source.
problems.verificationNote: The source reports a Lean check while the Erdős Problems community status remains pending; status therefore remains candidate.

problems.name: Erdős Problem #7
problems.statement: Can there be a finite covering system of the integers with distinct moduli, all odd and greater than one?
problems.claimIssueNote: The claimed Lean proof was withdrawn after an audit found an invalid central axiom and a statement-fidelity gap.
problems.verificationNote: VibeMathed records the claim as retracted after audit.
